newsitem.title: USA: Group says sues N.J. on new school funding plan.
newsitem.headline: Group says sues N.J. on new school funding plan.

text.p: The Education Law Center said it plans to file a lawsuit Monday challenging the constitutionality of New Jersey's new formula for financing public school education.
The law, signed by Gov Christine Whitman on Dec 20, seeks to address a court mandate that the state equalize spending between rich and poor districts.
But the Center said in a statement the new formula does not comply with earlier court rulings that spending in poor districts be equalized.

"(The new law) doesn't even try to eliminate the remaining 12 percent disparity in regular education spending," the center said. "In fact, disparity will grow because the law creates a two-tiered funding system. More affluent suburban districts can maintain current programs and spending while the urban districts are effectively locked-in to a level that is approximately $1,000 per-pupil lower."

The center also argued that academic standards established by Whitman would not on their own assure disadvantaged students an education that would allow them to compete with other students, as previous court rulings mandated.

The center said it would ask the court to order legislation be passed by June 30 that assures equivalent expenditures among districts for the 1997-1998 school year, or a redistribution of state aid to achieve that goal the following year.
A spokeswoman for Whitman said the governor would make a statement about the lawsuit later Monday.
